question: Should OpenClaw core accept model-elected continuation/delegate/compaction primitives with optional trusted cross-session enrichment, and under what rollout contract?
rationale: The branch adds model-controlled scheduling, persisted post-compaction handoff, and trusted cross-session system-event injection; code review can verify gates, but only maintainers can decide whether this belongs in core and what security/product boundary is acceptable.

options.title: Accept After Approval And Proof
options.body: Approve the core feature direction only after conflicts/mergeability are refreshed, exact-head real behavior proof covers the remaining paths, and the trust-boundary review is explicit.

options.title: Narrow To Same-Session Pilot
options.body: Require the PR to remove or defer cross-session trusted enrichment and land a smaller default-off same-session continuation pilot first.

options.title: Pause For Design
options.body: Keep or close the PR as not ready until a separate RFC settles the core versus plugin boundary and security model.

recommendation.title: Accept After Approval And Proof
recommendation.body: Approve the core feature direction only after conflicts/mergeability are refreshed, exact-head real behavior proof covers the remaining paths, and the trust-boundary review is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed this PR's continuation shape and explicitly called out the cross-session targeting policy as maintainer-owned.
